316557.literal:
Let $X$ be a finite list of vectors of rank $n$. Define the set of very short $X$-sets by

$$
S_-(X)=\{Y\subset X:\operatorname{rank}(X\setminus(Y\cup\{x\}))=n\text{ for every }x\in X\setminus Y\}.
$$

Let ${\cal P}_-(X)$ be the internal ${\cal P}$-space. **Very short sets conjecture.** For every $X$,

$$
{\cal P}_-(X)=\operatorname{span}\{p_Y:Y\in S_-(X)\}.
$$

The right-hand side is the earlier formulation of the internal ${\cal P}$-space and is already known from the supplied context to be a subspace of ${\cal P}_-(X)$; the conjecture asserts the reverse inclusion, so that the two variants coincide.

316630.literal:
Let $G\leq S_n$ be a permutation group, let $H\leq G$ be a subgroup, and let $P(G)$ and $P(H)$ denote the associated permutation polytopes. For a partition

$$
[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}=\bigsqcup_i I_i,
$$

write

$$
\operatorname{stab}(G;(I_i)_i):=\{\sigma\in G:\sigma(I_i)=I_i\text{ for all }i\}\leq G.
$$

**Stabilizer characterization conjecture.** If $P(H)\preceq P(G)$ is a face, then

$$
H=\operatorname{stab}(G;(I_i)_i)
$$

for some partition $[n]=\bigsqcup_i I_i$.

The paper notes that stabilizers of partitions provide an obvious class of subgroups whose permutation polytopes are faces. The conjecture asks whether every subgroup yielding a face arises this way; its resolution is not given.

321134.literal:
Let $S_k$ denote the set of permutations of length $k$, and let $alpha_p(n)$ be the number of permutations of length $n$ avoiding the consecutive pattern $p$. For a fixed pattern length $k$, write

$$
sigma=1 2 ldots k.
$$

**Elizalde–Noy maximality conjecture.** The increasing pattern $\sigma$ is the maximal pattern, in the sense that

$$
\alpha_{\sigma}(n) \geq \alpha_p(n)
$$

for all $p\in S_k$ and all $n$. This conjecture concerns the extremal enumeration of consecutive pattern avoidance; the source attributes it to Elizalde and Noy and gives no resolution.

Let $\widehat{W}^{\circ}$ be the finite subset of an affine Weyl group used in the moment-graph construction, let $\mathcal{B}(w)$ be the indecomposable object associated with $w\in\widehat{W}^{\circ}$, and let $\underline{\mathrm{rk}}\mathcal{B}(w)^x$ denote the graded rank of its $x$-component. Let $C'_w$ be the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis element and $T_x$ the standard Hecke-algebra basis element. **Fiebig's conjecture.**

$$
C'_w=\sum_{x}\underline{\mathrm{rk}}\mathcal{B}(w)^xT_x\quad\text{for all }w\in\widehat{W}^{\circ}.
$$

The paper states that this conjecture implies Lusztig's conjecture for the dual group and later proves that it is equivalent to affine Soergel's $p$-conjecture. Its resolution is therefore tied to the corresponding positive-characteristic Soergel-bimodule statement.

$$
\mathcal{C}(G_i,S_i)

form a family of $\epsilon$-expanders for some fixed $\epsilon>0$. The theorem proved in the paper establishes this for alternating and symmetric groups. 380081.literal:
Let $\mathcal{I}_n$ be the set of involutions in $\mathfrak{S}_n$, and define

$$
I_n(t)=\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{I}_n}t^{\operatorname{des}(\pi)}.
$$

**Guo–Zeng conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist coefficients $a_{n,i}\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
I_n(t)=\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor}a_{n,i}t^i(1+t)^{n-1-2i},
$$

where $0\leq i\leq\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor$.

This is a gamma-positivity expansion for the descent polynomial of involutions. The source presents it as an open problem after noting that unimodality and symmetry were already known.

380415.literal:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the set of exponential growth constants arising from hereditary properties of ordered graphs. For each real number $c$, consider the interval immediately to its right.

**No-accumulation-from-above conjecture.** For every $c\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(c)$ such that

$$
\mathcal{S}\cap(c,c+\varepsilon)=\emptyset.
$$

In particular, $\mathcal{S}$ has no accumulation points from above.

This is the proposed general “jump everywhere” principle for the possible exponential speeds. The supplied text gives no resolution.
